A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same work. All 16 pages of v1 and 17 pages of v2, including equations, tables, figures, and appendices, were readable and matched across renumbering and relocation.

before.justification: v1 reports original attention-decomposition analyses, positional-perturbation experiments, Qasper accuracy results in Table 1, and attention-feature visualizations.

after.justification: v2 retains those empirical results and adds a random-initialization experiment and quantitative long-context comparisons in Table 2.

M1.justification: The three-axis regression, controlled-distance decomposition, and query/key mechanism remain unchanged. The added controls and ALiBi discussion do not introduce a new algorithm. Attention acceleration, cache compression, and bias mitigation are proposed future applications.

E1.justification: The text-perturbation, ArXiv language-modeling, Qasper question-answering, and length-generalization coverage is retained. v2 names Pile for the existing Figure 6 analysis without establishing a dataset replacement or expansion. New model controls and length settings remain within the existing task coverage.

E2.justification: v2 adds a randomly initialized Llama-3.2-3B control for decomposition and an explicit LM-Infinite versus Extending Vanilla LM comparison in Table 2. These introduce substantive comparisons for two central explanations that lacked these reported controls in v1. InfLLM remains discussed but has no Table 2 results.

E3.justification: New evaluations include the random-initialization control on a 4096-token input and a length sweep at 4200, 5120, 6144, 7168, and 8192 tokens. Table 2 introduces feature-distribution KL divergence using multivariate Gaussian approximations alongside log-perplexity. The retained perturbation protocols are unchanged.

E4.justification: The random-initialization analysis tests whether decomposition follows automatically from architecture. Table 2 adds quantitative distribution-shift analysis and relates it to language-model loss, extending v1's PCA visualization in Figure 6. These materially strengthen the range of analyses addressing the central mechanism.

E5.justification: Section 3.2 newly identifies 0.9470 as an average across layers and reports a layerwise range of 0.914–0.967. This adds descriptive variability reporting, not repeated-run uncertainty. No seed counts, confidence intervals, or significance tests are added; the existing tokenwise standard-deviation visualizations remain unchanged.

E6.justification: v2 adds the random-model correlation of 0.028, layerwise correlation extrema, and Table 2's length-dependent results. At 8192 tokens, LM-Infinite versus vanilla has KL divergence 4.4401 versus 15.9810 and log-perplexity 1.004 versus 8.901. These are newly reported comparisons; Table 1 and the earlier correlations of 0.8650, 0.9470, and 0.959 remain unchanged.

T1.justification: New Theorem 1 and Appendix E formalize v1's informal RoPE expressivity assertion through a bounded-function approximation statement and Fourier-based derivation claiming an exponential remainder. The existing asymptotic disentanglement theorem, assumptions, and Appendix C proof are retained with renumbering.

C1.justification: The abstract and introduction retain the same principal claims: learned position–semantic disentanglement, its query/key mechanism, and explanations of positional robustness and length generalization. The conclusion preserves these contributions; its added application ideas are framed as future possibilities.

C2.justification: v2 explains how the decomposition applies to ALiBi, connects the new KL/loss comparison to distribution preservation, and discusses potential attention efficiency, KV-cache compression, and position-bias mitigation. The existing limitations concerning task complexity and acquisition during training are unchanged.

D1.justification: v2 specifies that the fixed query in Section 3.2 comes from the document's last token and identifies Pile for the retained PCA analysis. It also documents the Gaussian approximation used in Table 2. These are additional disclosures; the existing solver and regularization details remain unchanged.

R1.justification: v2 adds Nissilä on Fourier decay, the MPT reference, and Liu and Wang on position-related biases, supporting the new proof and application discussion. The main research positioning remains stable. The two Gao entries refer to the same Pile work and do not constitute two distinct additions.

P1.justification: v2 adds a nontriviality discussion, a short ALiBi subsection, and future-application bullets, with corresponding section and theorem renumbering. It also makes local explanatory and punctuation edits. Most prose and the overall narrative structure are retained.

P2.justification: v2 adds the full-width Table 2 and reflows Table 1 and surrounding text. Figures 1–9 retain their visual content, including identical Appendix D visualization pages; caption cross-references are updated. There is no substantial visual redesign.

improvement.justification: The random-initialization control and Table 2 improve empirical support beyond v1's largely qualitative treatment of these questions. However, the new Appendix E proof defines k(x) using a coefficient depending jointly on x and y without establishing independence from y, leaving Theorem 1 unsupported as written. The empirical gains and added theoretical reliability problem prevent a confident net quality judgment.
